children.name: Stercorarius
children.description: Piratical seabirds that relentlessly pursue other birds until they drop or disgorge their food. The Long-tailed Skua breeds on Swedish mountain tundra; the others are passage migrants offshore. Dark and pale morphs occur in several species.

children.name: Stercorarius parasiticus
children.description: The parasitic jaeger or arctic skua, also known as the parasitic skua or arctic jaeger, is a seabird in the skua family Stercorariidae. It is a migratory species breeding in Northern Fennoscandia, Scotland, Iceland, Greenland, Northern Canada, Alaska, and Siberia and wintering across the southern hemisphere. Kleptoparasitism is a major source of food for this species during migration and winter, and is where the name is derived from.

children.name: Stercorarius pomarinus
children.description: The pomarine jaeger, pomarine skua, or pomatorhine skua, is a seabird in the skua family Stercorariidae. It is a migrant, wintering at sea in the tropical oceans.

children.name: Stercorarius longicaudus
children.description: The long-tailed jaeger or long-tailed skua is a seabird in the skua family Stercorariidae.

children.name: Stercorarius skua
children.description: The great skua (Stercorarius skua), sometimes known by the name bonxie in Britain, is a large seabird in the skua family Stercorariidae.

children.name: Stercorarius maccormicki
children.description: The south polar skua (Stercorarius maccormicki) is a large seabird in the skua family, Stercorariidae.

children.name: Stercorarius chilensis
children.description: The Chilean skua, also known as the cinnamon skua (Stercorarius chilensis), is a large predatory seabird, which breeds in Argentina and Chile, but ranges as far north as Brazil and Peru when not breeding.
